title: Danantara Demands AI Data Centers Self-Power; OpenAI Safety Gaps Confirmed
dek: Indonesia's sovereign wealth vehicle shifts AI infrastructure risk to developers while external auditors confirm structural weaknesses in OpenAI's safety monitoring, tightening two converging pressures on the AI buildout.
summary: Danantara Indonesia has formally required AI data center projects to build their own power sources, a policy shift that transfers grid risk to private developers and complicates the $360-400 billion AI economic potential Indonesia's government is simultaneously promoting. External evaluators commissioned by OpenAI found material flaws in its AI monitoring system, adding independent evidence to a structural safety theme that has run for weeks. On Indonesia's energy reliability, IESR's two-year assessment of the Prabowo-Gibran administration calls fuel shortages and repeated blackouts in 2026 a systemic failure, not a logistics anomaly, a verdict that now frames the incoming PLN director Suroso Isnandar's mandate. The PPh 0% tax incentive for BUMN restructuring remains blocked pending two implementing regulations, keeping Danantara's consolidation pipeline frozen. Taken together, these signals show that Indonesia's AI and energy ambitions are colliding with infrastructure and governance bottlenecks that no single ministry controls.

signals.headline: IESR's two-year assessment labels 2026 fuel shortages and blackouts a systemic failure, not logistics
signals.whatChanged: IESR published a formal evaluation on 20 October 2026 of Indonesia's energy sector performance under two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration. The institute characterizes repeated blackouts and fuel shortages throughout 2026 as evidence of systemic failure in energy supply management, not as isolated distribution disruptions. A separate IESR statement on 19 October expressed solidarity with communities affected by haze and fuel scarcity simultaneously.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the pln-grid-investment thread and elevates it from operational complaint to governance verdict. IESR is Indonesia's most cited independent energy policy institute, and its framing as systemic failure, rather than transitional disruption, sets the analytical baseline for COP31 negotiations in November and for the incoming PLN director Suroso Isnandar's agenda. Kementerian ESDM's own communications during the same period focused on logistics remediation, deploying seven ships to Bali to extend fuel reserves to 15 days, which IESR's framing implicitly rejects as insufficient response.
signals.secondOrder: If the systemic failure diagnosis holds in the COP31 pre-negotiation period, Indonesia's credibility as a bankable energy transition partner weakens. Concessional financing instruments tied to performance milestones, including JETP commitments, depend on demonstrated institutional capacity. Repeated supply failures documented by a credible domestic institute give bilateral partners and multilateral lenders grounds to tighten conditionality or delay disbursement.
signals.action: Before COP31 in November, assess whether Indonesia's JETP implementation plan contains any energy reliability milestones that the documented 2026 failures would put at risk, and identify which bilateral partners have disbursement triggers linked to those milestones.

signals.headline: PPh 0% BUMN restructuring incentive remains blocked as two implementing regulations are still pending
signals.whatChanged: As of 23 October 2026, the PPh 0% tax incentive designed to facilitate BUMN asset consolidation under Danantara has not taken effect because the required Government Regulation (PP) and Ministry of Finance Regulation (PMK) have not been issued. Bloomberg Technoz and CNBC Indonesia both reported this regulatory gap, with Direktorat Jenderal Pajak confirming it is waiting for the PP and PMK before the incentive can be applied.
signals.whyItMatters: This is the same danantara-bumn-karya-restructuring thread, now 29 occurrences deep and at structural status. The incentive was announced as a mechanism to allow BUMN mergers and asset transfers without triggering large tax charges, which would otherwise make consolidation economically unattractive. Without the PP and PMK, no restructuring transaction can legally use the incentive, freezing the pipeline of planned mergers at the moment when Danantara's capital deployment ambitions, including hotel acquisitions in Makkah and AI infrastructure conditions, are accelerating.
signals.secondOrder: The divergence between Danantara's outward deal activity and the frozen domestic restructuring pipeline creates governance opacity. External investors see acquisition announcements while the internal BUMN consolidation that would rationalize the portfolio and reduce contingent liabilities remains stalled. This asymmetry raises the probability that Danantara's balance sheet exposure grows faster than its ability to integrate or exit legacy SOE positions.
signals.action: Track the Sekretariat Negara and DJP legislative calendar for the PP and PMK drafts. Any BUMN merger or asset transfer announced before those regulations are issued should be assessed for whether it can legally proceed without the tax incentive, and what the tax cost of proceeding early would be.

signals.headline: Danantara requires AI data center projects to build their own power supply, shifting grid risk to developers
signals.whatChanged: Danantara Indonesia has stated that AI data center projects seeking its involvement must provide their own energy sources rather than drawing on PLN's grid, according to CNN Indonesia reporting on 22 October 2026.
signals.whyItMatters: This continues the danantara-bumn-karya-restructuring thread and adds a new dimension: Danantara is not merely a passive capital allocator but is setting infrastructure conditions that redirect power procurement risk away from the state. Combined with the government's concurrent claim of a Rp 7,221 trillion AI economic opportunity by 2030, the policy creates a structural tension. Developers who want sovereign backing must solve the power problem independently, raising project costs and narrowing the viable investor pool.
signals.secondOrder: If self-power requirements become standard for sovereign-backed AI infrastructure in Indonesia, the market will bifurcate between projects with dedicated captive generation and those that cannot secure it. Captive power for data centers at scale almost certainly means gas turbines or co-located renewables, pulling demand away from PLN offtake agreements and reducing PLN's ability to cross-subsidize grid expansion from anchor industrial customers. The grid investment shortfall IESR has documented then deepens rather than resolves.
signals.action: Map which energy sources are technically and regulatorily feasible for captive AI data center power in Indonesia: geothermal, gas-fired co-generation, and large-scale solar with storage. Assess whether existing PLN power purchase agreement frameworks allow developers to bypass grid offtake, and identify which regulatory approvals from KESDM are required for self-supply schemes above 10 MW.
